warning: This is a relative heat-exposure index on a 0-1 scale derived from land class, sky view and shade. It is NOT degrees Celsius and NOT a modelled air-temperature field. Do not present it as either.

anchoring.warning: Anchored to a cited air-temperature band: HKO Lau Fau Shan station, July 2015-2024 (HKO_air: 26.4-32.7 C). This is a stated band for a Hong Kong summer, not a measurement of this site -- the station is ~20 km away. The field remains a relative 0-1 index, never degrees Celsius. Screening-level; relative, not absolute.

svf.method: Per-cell sky view factor from a horizon search over the massing height raster: SVF = 1 - (1/N) sum_i sin(gamma_i), where gamma_i is the horizon elevation angle in azimuth bin i (16 bins), searched to a 300 m (60-cell) radius. A cell under massing is inside the building and scores 0.
svf.limitation: Geometry, not radiation. SVF is a sky-exposure fraction -- how much sky a ground point sees -- not a temperature. No sun, no surface energy balance, no air temperature. The horizon is sampled on 16 azimuth rays, so a narrow slot between two buildings can fall between rays and be missed.
svf.warning: Heat is not a temperature. This is a relative heat-exposure index on a 0-1 scale derived from land class, sky view and shade -- not degrees Celsius and not a modelled air-temperature field. Screening-level; relative, not absolute.

assumptions.heatwaveNote: A display transform on the same field, not a scenario. Compare runs at the same stretch setting.

landClassProvenance: ESA WorldCover 10 m v200 (2021), CC BY 4.0, tiles ['N21E111', 'N21E114'], resampled to 5 m by nearest neighbour. See data/landcover_hsk.json for the ESA->ours class mapping.
